Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30-billion parameter open model designed specifically for persistent AI agents.
The model excels at multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and 8VC.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google's updated privacy policy allows Gmail data to be used for advertising.
The feature 'Personal Intelligence' is the mechanism enabling this increased data collection.
This represents a significant shift in how user data is leveraged for targeted advertising.

stories.title: Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Intel secured a waiver concerning potential US restrictions on foreign-made robotic vehicles.
The waiver addresses concerns that a fuzzy US ban could negatively impact semiconductor fabrication plants (fabs).
Intel asserts that foreign-made robotic vehicles are essential components for maintaining US chip production capabilities.

stories.title: Speech models in Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to include support for speech models.
The initial model featured is Phonon from Gradium, enabling text-to-speech functionality.
The implementation offers high performance, streaming audio over 100x faster than real-time on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the local and cloud deployment capabilities of the Ollama platform.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on the Ollama platform.
Beam is specifically designed for complex tasks such as software engineering, reasoning, and agentic workflows.
The model is offered for free, but only for a limited promotional period via Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local AI models within cloud environments.
The integration allows AI agents to run safely on Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, deployable AI agent solutions.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
Decision models provide probabilistic answers to questions, choices, and scoring requests.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Zen Browser is the Arc replacement I was looking for
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Zen Browser is being positioned as a potential successor to the discontinued Arc browser.
Arc browser was acquired by Atlassian, which has since shifted focus to developing Dia.
The narrative highlights the industry trend of browser evolution towards more AI-centric designs.

stories.title: A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature
stories.author: Tereza Ondráčková, wired.com
bullet_points: New modeling suggests Mars could possess unique ice-forming physics.
The potential discovery relates to physical phenomena never directly observed on Earth.
The research points toward a large-scale, distant scientific investigation (1,000-mile cloud).

stories.title: NASA updates lander plans for Moon landings, finally solves long-festering Orion issue
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: NASA is updating its lander plans for future Moon missions.
A long-standing technical issue concerning the Orion spacecraft has reportedly been resolved.
The project has secured the necessary mandate, resources, and stakeholder support.

stories.title: Hegseth warns prediction market bets warp military judgment, endanger troops
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Pentagon memo highlights the risk of insider trading providing adversaries with sensitive military intelligence.
The warning specifically addresses how prediction market betting could potentially warp military judgment.
The issue raises concerns about the security implications of financial speculation intersecting with defense operations.

stories.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
stories.author: Shenji Wan
bullet_points: SceneBloom is a new agentic framework designed to generate realistic and diverse indoor environments for training embodied AI agents.
It addresses the challenge of spatial grounding by combining visual layout sampling with contract-guided 3D scene construction.
The work aims to bridge the gap between rich visual priors from generative models and the need for physically valid, simulation-ready 3D environments.

stories.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
stories.author: Laixi Shi
bullet_points: Introduces RobustRLlib, a unified library and benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Addresses key limitations in existing robust RL: poor algorithm reusability and unclear empirical capability boundaries.
Integrates 17 representative robust online algorithms to facilitate broader research and deployment.

stories.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: DexPort is a new portable interface designed to solve the bottleneck of collecting high-quality data for dexterous manipulation.
It addresses limitations of existing methods, such as the complexity of teleoperation setups and the need for motion estimation from human demonstrations.
The tool allows for direct, easy data collection of executable robot actions using a hand-held interface.

stories.title: Beyond Discrete Tokens: Preserving Numerical Continuity in Medical Vision-Language Models
stories.author: Zhongliang Jiang
bullet_points: Introduces HAD-VLM, a novel hybrid framework for medical vision-language modeling.
Addresses the technical challenge of integrating continuous quantitative measurements with discrete token-based LLMs.
Utilizes a combination of autoregressive text generation and diffusion models, enhanced by visual prompt tuning for ultrasound images.

stories.title: Monetizing Intelligence: Advertising and Subscription Design on LLM Platforms
stories.author: Tianjun Feng
bullet_points: Examines the economic trade-offs for LLM platforms integrating advertising and subscription models.
Models a monopolistic platform optimizing response quality, ad intensity, and subscription pricing.
Suggests advertising can potentially finance useful service when ad-supported and ad-free tiers coexist.

stories.title: Yalda-Embedding: Open Development of a Competitive Persian Retrieval Model
stories.author: Armon Rasooli
bullet_points: Introduces Yalda Embedding, a new Persian retrieval model designed to address resource limitations in the language.
The model is an adaptation of Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, trained on over one million Persian query-document pairs.
Yalda Embedding achieved the highest macro-average among evaluated 0.6B models across eight Persian retrieval tasks from FaMTEB.

stories.title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
stories.author: Bernhard Bauer
bullet_points: The study empirically challenges the assumption that performance optimization via LLMs automatically leads to lower energy consumption.
It investigates whether LLM-optimized code is energy-efficient compared to traditional human-written reference solutions.
The research also assesses the energy overhead associated with the LLM self-refinement optimization process itself.

stories.title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Tajana Rosing
bullet_points: NgramRL addresses the high computational cost (over 70% of training time) associated with autoregressive rollout generation in RL post-training for LLMs.
The paper introduces a novel approach that integrates N-gram speculative decoding, specifically designed to handle the challenges of evolving policies in RL settings.
It aims to overcome limitations of existing speculative decoding methods, such as GPU memory consumption in model-based drafters and lack of repetition exploitation in model-free methods.

stories.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
stories.author: Laixi Shi
bullet_points: Introduces RobustRLlib, a unified library and benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Addresses key limitations in current robust RL research: limited algorithm reusability and unclear empirical boundaries.
Integrates 17 representative robust online RL algorithms to facilitate broader research and deployment.

stories.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: DexPort introduces a portable interface designed to address the bottleneck of collecting high-quality data for dexterous manipulation tasks.
It aims to bridge the gap between complex robot teleoperation setups and the limitations of using raw human demonstrations.
The technology facilitates direct, hands-on data collection for training AI models on fine motor skills.

stories.title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
stories.author: Egor Bondarev
bullet_points: Flownomaly addresses few-shot anomaly detection in industrial settings, a challenging area requiring modeling normality from limited examples.
The method reframes the problem as 'normal-counterpart recovery' within the frozen DINOv2 feature space.
It utilizes conditional flow matching over patch tokens to learn a velocity field, guiding noise toward the normal data distribution.

stories.title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox
stories.author: Federico Lucca
bullet_points: Introduces 'Foyer,' a self-hosted personal inbox agent designed for multilingual message routing and decision-making.
Addresses a critical gap in ML evaluation by proposing a rigorous measurement protocol to establish ground truth *before* training.
Compares a new Typed Decision Model against a classical baseline and a Generative LLM for inbox triage tasks.

stories.title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Ruosong Wang
bullet_points: The paper addresses instability in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for Large Language Models (LLMs) caused by discrepancies between inference and training implementations.
It proposes a novel solution: aligning only selected parts of the execution stack, rather than the entire stack or changing global precision.
This method aims to stabilize BF16 RL training even when other implementation differences persist between training and inference environments.

stories.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
stories.author: Thierry Tambe
bullet_points: Addresses the brittleness of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in robotic manipulation when encountering out-of-distribution states.
Introduces 'Backtrack,' a lightweight mechanism for failure detection and recovery in frozen VLAs.
The method avoids traditional costly solutions like recovery demonstrations or full policy retraining.

stories.title: Learning Positive Linear Combinations of ReLUs in Fully Polynomial Time
stories.author: Nikos Zarifis
bullet_points: The research addresses the PAC learning problem for positive linear combinations of ReLU activations in $\mathbb{R}^d$.
The authors present the first algorithm capable of solving this learning task in fully polynomial time.
The algorithm's complexity is polynomial in the dimension ($d$), the number of activations ($k$), and the desired accuracy ($1/\epsilon$).

stories.title: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
stories.author: Brian DePasquale
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenging problem of state inference and parameter learning in nonlinear filtering.
It focuses on solving the Zakai equation, a high-dimensional Stochastic Partial Differential Equation (SPDE) governing the unnormalized filtering distribution.
The proposed method, ZENO, utilizes Neural Operators to tackle the computational intractability of these SPDEs, relevant to scientific ML in engineering and neuroscience.

stories.title: The Language of Instruction: Genre and Generative AI
stories.author: James E. Dobson
bullet_points: The paper proposes that instruction-fine-tuned language models operate within a specific 'instructional-conversational genre'.
This genre is defined as a blend of discursive language derived from recursive interactions between humans and generative models.
The implementation of this genre is achieved through instruction fine-tuning, system prompts, and formalized input structures.

stories.title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox
stories.author: Federico Lucca
bullet_points: Introduces 'Foyer,' a self-hosted personal inbox agent designed for multilingual message routing and triage.
Addresses a critical gap in AI evaluation by proposing a rigorous measurement protocol to establish ground truth *before* model training.
Compares typed decision models against a classical baseline and a Generative LLM for inbox management tasks.

stories.title: Yalda-Embedding: Open Development of a Competitive Persian Retrieval Model
stories.author: Armon Rasooli
bullet_points: Introduces Yalda Embedding, a new competitive dense retrieval model specifically for the Persian language.
The model is an adaptation of Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and was trained on over one million Persian query-document pairs.
It achieves the highest macro-average among evaluated 0.6B models on eight Persian retrieval tasks from FaMTEB, addressing resource limitations in the field.

stories.title: Do "True" and "False" Add Up to One? Complement Consistency in LLM-Agent Opinion Simulations
stories.author: Jin Qi
bullet_points: The research investigates 'Complement Consistency' in LLM-agent opinion simulations.
It tests a theoretical property: if an agent's state represents its opinion, flipping the claim (to its complement) should result in probabilities summing to one (p vs. 1-p).
This work explores the internal consistency and logical behavior of opinion dynamics modeled by LLMs.

stories.title: J-Comm: Jacobian-Guided Latent Communication between LLM Agents
stories.author: Saman Halgamuge
bullet_points: Introduces J-Comm, a framework designed to enable latent communication between Large Language Model (LLM) agents.
Features GEAR (Geometric Agreement for Latent Reasoning), a training-free method that reweights token candidates to optimize geometric consensus in embedding space.
The framework addresses the need for an interface allowing external models to leverage an LLM's intermediate reasoning computations.

stories.title: Interpretable sparse fine-tuning with TopKLoRA enables faithful circuit discovery
stories.author: Constantin Venhoff
bullet_points: Addresses the security risk of model backdoors introduced by poisoned training data.
Introduces TopKLoRA, an interpretable variant of LoRA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
Aims to make the parameter changes during fine-tuning transparent, aiding in backdoor localization.

stories.title: Communicating with the Entire Population: Machine Translation of Emergency Alerts and Warnings
stories.author: William D. Lewis
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for multilingual communication during emergencies to reach all affected populations.
It investigates the reliability and adequacy of using commercial Machine Translation tools in high-stakes emergency alert scenarios.
The study involves a nationwide survey of emergency managers to gauge their confidence and concerns regarding automated translation outputs.

stories.title: About the compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs
stories.author: support.apple.com via freddyb
bullet_points: The news concerns the compromise of intermediate Certificate Authorities (CAs) belonging to eMudhra.
This is a significant cybersecurity incident impacting digital trust infrastructure.
The source (Lobsters) suggests a technical discussion or analysis of the vulnerability.

stories.title: How to Measure AI Search Visibility Beyond Rankings and Clicks
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: Traditional SEO metrics (rankings, clicks) are insufficient for measuring visibility in the age of AI search.
AI-generated search answers present a new challenge to traditional digital marketing measurement.
The article discusses methods to track brand presence when appearing within AI-generated summaries.
